vo.fehler.vorschub: The tool controller has no feed rate.
vb.fehler.werte: Cutter, step-down and feed per revolution must be greater than 0.
vb.fehler.steigung: The feed per revolution is larger than the cutter – ridges would remain.
vb.fehler.platz: There is no room for the cutter between chuck and part.
vb.fehler.platz_halter: There is no room for the cutter's holder between chuck and part.
vb.hinten_frei: The cutter cannot reach the last {laenge} in front of the chuck – material stays there. A larger part-off width helps.
vb.fehler.schrittweite: Cutter and stepover must be greater than 0.
vb.fehler.schrittweite_gross: The stepover is larger than the cutter – ridges would remain between the passes.
vb.fehler.muster: Finishing does not know the pattern “{muster}” – spiral or lines along the axis.
vf.fehler.fehlt: The selected faces {namen} no longer exist in the model – select them again in the wizard.
vf.fehler.nicht_erreichbar: None of the selected faces can be reached from outside – they lie under an overhang or across the axis.
va.kopf.bearbeitung: Step 2 of 2: what do you want to do?
va.weiter.tooltip: On to step 2: what you want to do with the bar – rough it all round, say.
va.zurueck.tooltip: Back to step 1: bar, centre, rotary axis.
va.schruppen.tooltip: Creates the operation “All-round roughing”. Unticked, “Create” only creates job and bar.
va.schruppen.text: Removes the bar all round down to the finishing allowance: in layers, with a cutter pointing at the axis from outside while the rotary axis turns.
va.werkstoff.tooltip: Which material the cutting data are for – the stock's if it has one, otherwise the one used last.
va.fraeser.tooltip: A cutter from the tool manager with cutting data: end, torus, ball, slot or face mill.
va.fraeser.keiner: The tool manager has no cutter with cutting data for this material – add one there (“Tool manager …”).
va.werkzeugverwaltung.tooltip: Opens the tool manager. Once you save there, its cutters are available here.
va.flaechen.tooltip: Which faces are milled: without a selection all around – every outer face. Clicking a face of the part adds it, clicking again removes it.
va.flaechen.liste.tooltip: The selected faces: green reachable, yellow partly, red not – a tool pointing from outside at the axis cannot get there. Double-click removes a face.
va.flaechen.rundum: All around – every outer face. To mill single faces only: click them in 3D (clicking again removes them).
va.flaechen.alle: All outer faces selected – all around.
va.flaechen.nur: Only these faces: the cutter mills where it touches one of them; in between it lifts and re-enters safely.
va.flaechen.alle_knopf.tooltip: Selects every face that faces outwards – that is all around.
va.flaeche.quer: across the axis – formed with the neighbouring faces
va.flaeche.fehlt: no longer exists in the part
va.einsatz.tooltip: Which cutting data of the cutter apply – “Roughing” preselected. It gives spindle speed, feed and the suggestions for step-down and feed per revolution.
va.zustellung.tooltip: How deep each layer cuts, radially (ap). Empty uses the grey suggestion from the use case.
va.steigung.tooltip: How far the spiral advances along the bar per revolution (ae) – at most the cutter diameter. Empty uses the grey suggestion from the use case.
va.aufmass.tooltip: This much stays all round – for finishing.
va.ueberlauf.tooltip: This far the centre of the cutter runs behind the part, continuing the profile of the part's end straight: the rear edge gets finished, and when parting off the blade meets a straight piece instead of a slope it would wander on. Behind that the material stays – it holds the part. Suggestion: parting width + 0.5 mm.
va.abstand_futter.tooltip: How far the edge of the cutter stays in front of the chuck's clamping face – or that of its holder, if it reaches further beyond the tool axis. Suggestion 5 mm.
va.sicherheit.tooltip: How far above and in front of the bar the cutter moves in rapid. Suggestion 2 mm.
va.ausspannen: The bar has to stick out {laenge} {einheit} from the chuck: {teile}.
va.lagen.keine: Nothing to rough: the part already fills the bar.
va.radius: In the program X is the radius, not the diameter – on a lathe switch the program header to radius (Siemens DIAMOF). Feed is given as G93 (1 ÷ time).
va.radius_durchmesser: X is in the program as a diameter (Ø), as on your control; the check window shows it that way. FreeCAD's own post processors write X as a radius – the help (?) says what to do then.
va.schlichten.tooltip: Creates the operation “All-round finishing”: after roughing, one spiral – or lines along the axis – on the part.
va.schlichten.text: After roughing, runs one spiral on the part – or lines along the axis where the faces do not go all round – the tip on the surface plus allowance, calculated with the cutter's shape. The stepover comes from the tool table.
va.schlichtfraeser.tooltip: A cutter from the tool manager with cutting data whose shape the add-on knows: ball, torus, flat, tapered ball, lollipop, chamfer, radius, slitting, face or dovetail mill.
va.schlichteinsatz.tooltip: Which cutting data of the cutter applies – “Finishing” preselected. It gives speed, feed and the stepover (ae).
va.schlichtfraeser.keiner: The tool manager has no cutter “All-round finishing” can calculate with (with cutting data for this material) – add one there (“Tool manager …”).
va.schrittweite.tooltip: How far the spiral advances along the bar per revolution – for lines along the axis, how far apart they are on the largest radius – at most the cutter diameter. Empty: the grey suggestion, ae of the application from the tool table.
va.aufmass_schlichten.tooltip: This much stays all round after finishing – 0 finishes the part.
va.querachse.tooltip: The spiral uses all axes: at every point the tool axis stands along the surface normal. On a flat face the rotary axis holds and the cross axis drives the straight line – also where the face goes below the turning centre. With any cutter: an end or bull-nose mill lies flat on flat spots.
va.querachse.ohne_form: The add-on doesn't know this cutter's shape – then without the cross axis.
va.querachse.vorschlag_stirn: The machine has the cross axis: the cutter stands normal to the surface; on flat spots its face lies flat and drives the straight line with it, the rotary axis holds there.
va.querachse.schruppen.tooltip: The spiral of every layer uses all axes: the tool axis stands along the surface normal, on flat spots the rotary axis holds and the cross axis drives the straight line; per layer at most the step-down below the bar. The preview computes without the cross axis (layers and time almost the same).
va.querachse.schruppen.vorschlag: The machine has the cross axis: the layers follow the surface – on flat spots the cutter drives the straight line with it, the stock allowance stays even there.
va.querachse.nur_rundum: All round only – with selected faces roughing runs rows.
va.querachse.vorschlag: The machine has the cross axis; on flat spots the ball mill drives the straight line with it, the rotary axis holds there.
va.querachse.keine: {maschine} has no axis across the bar – the spiral runs with rotary axis and radius.
va.muster.tooltip: How the finishing path runs: as a spiral all round, or in lines along the axis at a fixed angle – for faces that do not go all round (flat, groove, cam). Suggested is what fits the selected faces; the reason is shown below.
va.muster.vorschlag.spirale: Suggestion: spiral – it goes all round.
va.muster.vorschlag.linien: Suggestion: lines along the axis – the selected faces do not go all round.
va.schlichten.schon: The job already has “{name}” – double-click it to change it.
va.plan.tooltip: Creates the operation “Indexed facing”: the rotary axis stands still, a flat face along the bar is milled in rows with the axis across the bar (Y for C), like face milling – flat right into the corners; a cross hole is milled in a helix or drilled with the drill (“Radial drilling”).
va.plan.text: Mills selected flat faces along the bar (flat, wrench flat, slot floor) flat: the rotary axis turns the face to the cutter, which runs rows along the axis with its flat tip, steps across by the row spacing and goes down in layers to the face. Selected cross holes are milled in a helix – or a drill of their diameter drills them. Needs an axis across the bar (Y for C).
va.planfraeser.tooltip: A cutter with a flat tip from the tool manager with cutting data: flat, torus or face mill.
va.planeinsatz.tooltip: Which cutting data of the cutter apply – “Facing” preselected. It gives speed, feed, stepdown (ap) and row spacing (ae).
va.planfraeser.keiner: The tool manager has no cutter with a flat tip and cutting data for this material – create one there (“Tool manager …”).
va.zustellung_plan.tooltip: This deep per layer, perpendicular to the face. Empty: the grey suggestion, ap of the application from the tool table.
va.zeilenabstand.tooltip: How far the rows step across (with Y for C) – at most as wide as the flat part of the tip. Empty: the grey suggestion, ae of the application from the tool table.
va.aufmass_plan.tooltip: This much stays on the face; 0 finishes it.
va.plan.nuten: – {n} of them as a slot: full width with the ramp or in arcs, the wall all round.
va.plan.bohrungen: – {n} of them as a hole across the bar: helix down, the wall all round (a through hole from both sides, each to the middle).
va.plan.vorschlag_mantel: Suggestion: on – a slot on the outside of the bar: {flaechen}. The rotary axis turns, the cutter runs along the slot – full width down the ramp, in rows to the walls if it is wider.
va.plan.vorschlag_gemischt: Suggestion: on – {flaechen}: each the way it needs – a flat face in rows into the corners, a slot on the outside along it, a cross hole in a helix or with the drill.
va.plan.mantelnuten: – {n} of them as a slot on the outside of the bar: the rotary axis turns, the cutter runs along the slot.
va.plan.mit_bohrer: Drill the cross holes with {bohrer} (own operation “Radial drilling”)
va.plan.mit_bohrer.tooltip: Besides the cutter, this drill drills the selected cross holes radially – faster than milling them in a helix. Off: the cutter mills the holes as well.
va.plan.nur_gleichlauf.tooltip: On: every row climb milling, from the front towards the chuck – at its end the cutter lifts and enters again at the front of the next; the rows across in the order that puts the material on the climb side. Off: back and forth, faster, but every other row conventional. With “Reverse” on the tool controller (M4) the order turns with it.
va.schruppen.nur_gleichlauf.tooltip: Only with selected faces: on, every row around the bar runs on its own, climb milling – at its end the cutter lifts and enters again at the next. Off: back and forth, faster, but every other row conventional. With “Reverse” on the tool controller (M4) the direction turns with it. All round without faces always runs the spiral, climb milling.
va.linien.nur_gleichlauf.tooltip: Only for “lines along the axis”: on, every line runs on its own, climb milling – at its end the cutter lifts and enters again at the start of the next; the surface becomes more even. Off: back and forth, faster. With “Reverse” on the tool controller (M4) the direction turns with it. The spiral always runs climb milling.
vp.fehler.mantel_breit: The cutter Ø {fraeser} is wider than the slot on the outside of the bar ({breite}) – choose a narrower one.
vp.fehler.mantel_kurz: The slot on the outside of the bar ({breite} wide) is too short around for the cutter – its tip would cut into the walls at its ends.
va.plan.vorschlag_bohrung: Suggestion: on – a hole across the bar: {flaechen}. The rotary axis faces its opening, the cutter goes down in a helix and round the wall.
va.plan.vorschlag_bohren: Suggestion: on – drill radially with {bohrer}: {flaechen}. The rotary axis faces its opening, the drill goes down – faster than milling.
va.plan.keine_ebene: Indexed facing needs a selected flat face along the bar facing outwards (flat, slot floor), a hole across the bar or the floor of a slot on the outside of the bar – click it in 3D.
va.plan.keine_querachse: Indexed facing needs an axis across the bar (Y for C) – “{maschine}” has none.
va.plan.vorschlag_rundum: With the cross axis, {flaechen} can be machined flat in rows – the rotary axis stands still, Y steps across, the cutter runs straight passes along. Tick it: “Finish all round” then leaves them out.
va.plan.schraeg: {flaeche} slopes along by {winkel}° – the rows follow it, also below the centre of rotation; last a finishing layer so dense that at most 0.01 mm stays between the rows (the flat end sits at an angle there: the machine has no swivel axis).
va.plan.vorschlag: Suggestion: on – flat along the bar: {flaechen}. This makes it flat right into the corners; with the cutter on the ray from the axis something would remain at the edge.
va.plan.schon: “{name}” already exists in the job – double-click it to change it.
va.entgraten.tooltip: Creates the operation “All-round deburring”: a chamfer mill runs along the outer edges of the selected faces (or a ball mill breaks them), the rotary axis turns with it.
va.entgraten.text: Breaks the outer edges of the selected faces – where they bend outwards into another face, also into the rest of the part: every point of the edge comes under the cutter, which sinks to the edge and the chamfer width deeper. Inner edges, fillets and the end faces front and rear stay (no burr; facing and parting come later).
va.entgratfraeser.tooltip: A chamfer mill from the tool manager with cutting data – or a ball mill that rounds the edge.
va.entgrateinsatz.tooltip: Which cutting data of the cutter apply – “Chamfering” preselected. It gives speed and feed.
va.entgratfraeser.keiner: The tool manager has no chamfer or ball mill with cutting data for this material – create one there (“Tool manager …”).
va.breite.tooltip: How wide the chamfer gets at a right-angled edge with a 90° chamfer mill (with a flat tip, wider by its radius on the flat side), or the edge break with a ball mill. Empty: 0.3 mm.
va.entgraten.ergebnis_ausgelassen: → {kanten} edges, about {zeit}; {ausgelassen} the cutter cannot reach
va.entgraten.kein_fraeser: All-round deburring needs a chamfer mill or ball mill with cutting data for this material in the tool manager.
va.entgraten.keine_kanten: The selected faces have no outer edge to deburr – inner edges and fillets have no burr, the end faces front and rear do not exist in the job yet.
va.entgraten.vorschlag: Suggestion: on – {kanten} outer edges on the selected faces, and the chamfer mill {werkzeug} is available.
va.entgraten.kugel: {kanten} outer edges on the selected faces; the tool manager has no chamfer mill – the ball mill {werkzeug} rounds the edges if you tick it.
va.entgraten.schon: “{name}” already exists in the job – double-click it to change it.
va.plan.kein_fraeser: Flat along the bar: {flaechen} – but the tool manager has no cutter with a flat tip and cutting data for this material; with one the wizard suggests “Indexed facing”.
va.rund: {art}: “All-round roughing” calculates as with an end mill of the same diameter – the part stays safe. Between the turns of the spiral, ridges up to {rille} mm above the allowance remain; less feed per revolution makes them flatter.
va.lage.nicht_radial: {werkzeug} does not sit radially on {aufnahme} – the path needs it radial from {richtung} towards the axis. Give {werkzeug} a holder that stands radially in the tool manager, such as “VDI30 driven radial”.
va.lage.nicht_radial_gerade: {werkzeug} does not sit radially on {aufnahme} – the path needs it radial from {richtung} towards the axis. {aufnahme} itself stands radially: give {werkzeug} a straight holder in the tool manager.
va.lage.kein_platz: “{maschine}” has no station for {werkzeug} – “Check on machine” skips it.
va.lage.alle_belegt: No station of “{maschine}” is free for {werkzeug} in this job – free one in the “Tool loading” window. Otherwise the program calls it by its number.
va.rund.ohne_rillen: {art}: “All-round roughing” calculates as with an end mill of the same diameter – the part stays safe; at this feed per revolution no ridges remain.
va.uebernehmen.tooltip: Changes the operation: cutter, application and the values below – one undo step. A tool controller that no operation uses afterwards is removed.
va.aendern.text: You are changing an existing machining: the cutter, the application and the values below apply after “Apply”. Speed and feed belong to the application in the tool manager – change and save them there, then “Apply”.
va.aendern.werkzeug_fehlt: The cutter of this machining (“{controller}”) is not on offer here – it is missing from the tool manager or has no cutting data there for this material. “Apply” uses the selected one.
va.aendern.zurueck: “Back” leads to bar, centre and rotary axis as they are in the job.
va.aendern.rohteil_fest: Bar and position can no longer be changed here: the job no longer looks as the wizard created it (stock or part changed by hand).
va.aendern.anderes_teil: While changing, the part stays “{teil}” – for another part create a new job: click its end face, then “4-axis machining”.
vs.name: All-round finishing {werkzeug}
vs.eigenschaft.schrittweite: Stepover: feed per revolution of the spiral, along the bar – for lines along the axis their spacing on the largest radius; at most the cutter diameter.
vs.eigenschaft.aufmass: Allowance: this much stays all round after finishing (0: finished).
vs.eigenschaft.muster: Pattern: spiral all round, or lines along the axis at a fixed angle – for faces that do not go all round.
vs.eigenschaft.rest_hoechstens: At most this much is left above the path after roughing – stock allowance, ridges and what its cutter could not reach; finishing takes it in one pass (calculated).
vb.rest_viel: After roughing up to {rest} is left above the path – finishing cuts that deep there in one pass; the roughing cutter got no closer.
vs.eigenschaft.querachse: The spiral with the cross axis (Y with C): at every point the tool axis stands along the surface normal – on a flat face the rotary axis holds, the cross axis drives the straight line. With any cutter whose shape the add-on knows.
vs.eigenschaft.kammhoehe: Height of the ridge left between two turns of the spiral, on a face square to the cutter (calculated).
vs.eigenschaft.umdrehungen: Number of turns of the spiral (calculated).
vs.eigenschaft.linien: How many lines along the axis the path has (calculated; 0 for the spiral).
vs.fehler.form: The add-on does not know the shape of this tool (thread mill, drill …) – choose a ball, torus or flat end mill for finishing.
vs.fehler.ohne_schruppen: The job has no “All-round roughing” – without it, finishing would take the whole bar in one pass.
vp.name: Indexed facing {werkzeug}
vp.eigenschaft.huebe: With the drill: how often it goes down into the cross holes, over all sides (calculated).
vp.fehler.keine_bohrung: None of the selected faces is a hole across the bar – a drill only drills those; for a flat face choose a cutter in “Indexed facing”.
vp.fehler.sack: The hole Ø {durchmesser} has a flat bottom – a drill would leave its point; choose a cutter in “Indexed facing” for it.
va.plan.ergebnis_bohren: → {bohrungen} drilled ({seiten}), {huebe}, about {zeit} – radially with the drill, pecking deeper than 3 × D; a through hole from both sides, each with the point past the middle.
va.plan.nur_bohrungen: The drill only drills the holes – the flat faces need a cutter (“Indexed facing” once more with it).
vp.eigenschaft.zustellung: Stepdown: at most this deep per layer, perpendicular to the face.
vp.eigenschaft.zeilenabstand: Row spacing: at most this far the rows step across (with Y for C) – at most as wide as the flat part of the tip.
vp.eigenschaft.aufmass: Allowance: this much stays on the face (0: finished).
vp.eigenschaft.ebenen: How many flat faces along the bar the operation mills (calculated).
vp.eigenschaft.lagen: How many layers the operation runs over all faces (calculated).
vp.eigenschaft.zeilen: How many rows the operation runs over all faces and layers (calculated).
vp.fehler.form: Indexed facing needs a cutter with a flat tip – flat, torus or face mill, not a ball mill.
vp.fehler.werte: Stepdown and row spacing must be greater than 0.
vp.fehler.zeilenabstand: The row spacing is wider than the flat part of the tip – material would remain between the rows.
vp.fehler.keine_ebene: None of the selected faces is a flat face along the bar facing outwards, a hole across the bar or the floor of a slot on the outside of the bar – indexed facing mills only those (a flat, the floor of a slot, a cross hole, a slot on the outside).
vp.fehler.nichts: Nothing is left above the selected faces – there is nothing to mill.
ve.name: All-round deburring {werkzeug}
ve.eigenschaft.breite: Chamfer width: how far the tip sinks below the contact at the edge – with a 90° chamfer mill at a right-angled edge the width of the chamfer (with a flat tip, more by its radius on the flat side); with a ball mill the width of the edge break.
ve.eigenschaft.kanten: How many edges the operation runs (calculated).
ve.eigenschaft.ausgelassen: How many edges the cutter cannot reach anywhere – in the shadow of a step, in a narrow slot, too close to the chuck (calculated).
ve.fehler.form: The add-on does not know the shape of this tool – choose a chamfer mill or a ball mill for deburring.
ve.fehler.breite: The chamfer width must be greater than 0.
ve.fehler.keine_kanten: The selected faces have no outer edge to deburr – inner edges and fillets have no burr, the end faces front and rear do not exist in the job yet (facing, parting).
ve.fehler.nichts: The cutter reaches none of the edges: they lie in the shadow of a step, in a narrow slot or too close to the chuck.
ve.ausgelassen: {anzahl} edges the cutter cannot reach (in the shadow of a step, in a narrow slot or too close to the chuck) – see the property “Ausgelassen”.
pf.name: Face milling {werkzeug}
pf.eigenschaft.flaechen: The selected flat faces facing up (“Face6” …): each is milled flat. Empty: the top of the part.
pf.eigenschaft.zustellung: Stepdown: at most this deep per layer.
pf.eigenschaft.zeilenabstand: Row spacing: at most this far the rows step across – at most as wide as the flat part of the tip.
pf.eigenschaft.aufmass: Allowance: this much stays on the face (0: finished).
pf.eigenschaft.richtung: Rows along X or Y, per face: both directions computed, the faster one taken.
pf.eigenschaft.ueberlauf: Overrun: how far the centre of the cutter runs past the face along the rows; 0: the suggestion, 0.6 × diameter.
pf.eigenschaft.sicherheit: Safety distance: the rapid down ends this far above the material.
pf.eigenschaft.austritt: This much of the feed (%) the row runs while leaving the stock – slower against the burr.
pf.eigenschaft.nur_gleichlauf: Every row climb milling: then lift and start again from the front – otherwise back and forth (every other row conventional).
pf.eigenschaft.ebenen: How many faces the operation mills (calculated).
pf.eigenschaft.lagen: How many layers the operation runs over all faces (calculated).
pf.eigenschaft.zeilen: How many rows the operation runs over all faces and layers (calculated).
pf.fehler.form: Face milling needs a cutter with a flat tip – flat, torus or face mill, not a ball mill.
pf.fehler.werte: Stepdown and row spacing must be greater than 0.
pf.fehler.zeilenabstand: The row spacing is wider than the flat part of the tip – material would remain between the rows.
pf.fehler.keine_ebene: None of the selected faces is a flat face facing up – face milling mills only those.
pf.fehler.nichts: Nothing stands above the selected faces – the stock does not reach above them.
pf.fehler.rohteil: The job has no stock – machining needs its top.
ko.name: Contour {werkzeug}
ko.eigenschaft.flaechen: The selected walls (“Face6” …): vertical faces with a horizontal bottom edge – the contour follows them.
ko.eigenschaft.zustellung: Stepdown: at most this deep per layer when roughing.
ko.eigenschaft.zeilenabstand: Row spacing: at most this far apart lie the roughing passes (sideways, ae).
ko.eigenschaft.aufmass: Allowance: this much stays on the wall after roughing – finishing takes it off.
ko.eigenschaft.schlichten: Finishing: afterwards once along the wall at the cutter radius, in one go over the full height (at most the cutting edge length per go).
ko.eigenschaft.breite: Width: this much material stands beside the wall – that many roughing passes. 0: as much as the stock says (everything to the edge, a pocket completely).
ko.eigenschaft.tiefer: Deeper: this much deeper than the bottom edge of the wall the contour goes – to cut free.
ko.eigenschaft.einfahrradius: Lead-in radius: the quarter circle with which the path enters and leaves the wall tangentially; 0: the cutter radius.
ko.eigenschaft.austritt: This much of the feed (%) the path runs when leaving the stock – slower against the burr.
ko.eigenschaft.konturen: This many contours (chains of walls) the operation runs (computed).
ko.eigenschaft.lagen: This many layers the operation runs over all contours, roughing and finishing (computed).
ko.eigenschaft.bahnen: This many passes the operation runs, each with lead-in and lead-out (computed).
ko.fehler.form: Contour needs a cutter with a flat tip – flat, torus or face mill, no ball mill.
ko.fehler.werte: Stepdown and row spacing must be greater than 0.
ko.fehler.zeilenabstand: The row spacing is wider than the cutter – material would remain between the roughing passes.
ko.fehler.keine_wand: None of the selected faces is a wall – a vertical face with a horizontal bottom edge. Contour follows such faces.
ko.fehler.nichts: Nothing stands beside the selected walls, or the cutter does not fit in – the stock does not reach past them, or the pocket is narrower than the cutter.
ra.name: Clearing {werkzeug}
ra.eigenschaft.flaechen: The selected flat upward faces (“Face6” …): each is cleared – the top from the outside inwards, a pocket floor from the inside outwards. Empty: the top of the part.
ra.eigenschaft.zustellung: Stepdown: at most this deep per layer – for clearing the full cutting edge length.
ra.eigenschaft.zeilenabstand: Stepover (ae): how far the rings move inwards – at most the cutter radius.
ra.eigenschaft.aufmass: Allowance: how much stays at walls and islands – for the contour.
ra.eigenschaft.aufmass_boden: Floor allowance: how much stays on the face (0: finished).
ra.eigenschaft.gleichlauf: Climb milling: the material to the right of the direction of travel (spindle clockwise, M3); otherwise conventional.
ra.eigenschaft.variante: The path: automatic (compute all; the fastest that keeps the load), “ringe” (the fastest of the rings, regardless of load), “adaptiv” (FreeCAD's adaptive core: keeps the engagement, hardly lifts), “rohteil” (rings from the stock edge inwards), “morph” (rings that get rounder towards the boss) or “inseln” (rings around islands and walls, from the outside inwards) – or “stiche” (Manuel's clearing: passes – the offsets of island or wall from the outside inwards, each in from the air, back at rapid – and rings where they close; only when chosen – without a choice the fastest that keeps the load wins).
ra.eigenschaft.laeufe: How many runs – a ring interrupted by an island is run in pieces (result).
ra.eigenschaft.gerechnet: The computed variants with their time, the chosen one first (result).
ra.fehler.form: Clearing needs a cutter with a flat tip – end mill, torus or face mill, not a ball mill.
ra.fehler.werte: Stepdown and stepover must be greater than 0.
ra.fehler.zeilenabstand: The stepover is larger than the cutter radius – when clearing, the rings move at most by the radius.
ra.fehler.keine_ebene: None of the selected faces is flat and upward – clearing needs a top face or a pocket floor.
ra.fehler.nichts: Nothing stands above the selected faces, or the cutter does not fit – the stock ends on the face, or the pocket is narrower than the cutter.
befehl.bearbeitung.tooltip: Mills a part in a block in three steps: click the face you want to machine – the add-on creates the job with the stock –, then choose the strategies and their cutters; “Create” creates the ticked operations. If such an operation is selected, the window opens for changing it.
ba.anleitung: Click the face you want to machine – then the add-on creates the job with the stock (“Cancel” removes it again).
ba.anleitung.job: The job with the stock has been created. If the part lies on the table differently than modelled: “Click face …”, then the face that lies at the bottom; ↺/↻ turns X by 90°. Check stock and origin, then “Next”.
ba.anleitung.was: Which faces are machined: a click on a face adds it or takes it out – flat ones facing up are faced, walls get the contour. Below, the strategies with their time; the fastest is ticked.
ba.anleitung.einstellungen: The values of the ticked strategies – preset from the tool manager, change them only where needed. “Create” puts them into the job.
ba.einstellungen.leer: No strategy is ticked in step 2.
ba.weiter.tooltip: To the next step. “Create” works already now – with the suggestions.
ba.zurueck.tooltip: To the step before – nothing is lost.
ba.aendern.text: You are changing “{name}”: faces, cutter, application and the values below apply after “Apply”. The stock stays as it is in the job.
ba.kein_dokument: Open the document with the part first.
ba.maschine.tooltip: Which machine you mill the part on – from your list (“Machines …”). The job remembers it: “Check on machine” uses it without asking.
ba.maschine.liste.tooltip: Your machines: add or build new ones – then they are offered here.
ba.maschine.leer: No machine chosen yet: “Machines …” takes yours. Until then the assistant assumes a 3-axis mill.
ba.maschine.nicht_gefunden: This machine's file is no longer there – in “Machines …”, “Find …” shows where it is now.
ba.maschine.vierachs.tooltip: Closes this assistant (the job is taken back) and opens the 4-axis assistant with the part, the clicked face and this machine – there the stock is a bar.
ba.maschine.drehmaschine: On the lathe the stock is a bar, not a block – the 4-axis assistant does that: “Continue in the 4-axis assistant”.
ba.maschine.rundachse: This mill has a rotary axis: for a round stock (bar) continue in the 4-axis assistant, for a block here.
ba.rohteil.teil.tooltip: A body you modelled as the stock – pre-machined, cast, welded. The job takes it as it lies relative to the part in the model.
ba.rohteil.teil.text: The body is the job's stock, as it lies relative to the part in the model; the paths use its outline and its top.
ba.rohteil.keine_teile: There is no other body in the document: model the stock as a body of its own (Part or PartDesign) – then it is offered here.
ba.unten.tooltip: Which face of the part lies on the table: in step 1 click a flat face in 3D – the part in the job turns so that it faces down; stock and origin follow. The model itself stays as it is.
ba.unten.waehlen.tooltip: Then click the face of the part in 3D that lies on the table – the part in the job turns so that it faces down.
ba.unten.zurueck.tooltip: The part lies in the job as it is modelled again.
ba.unten.nicht_eben: {name} is not flat – only a flat face can lie at the bottom.
ba.x.tooltip: Turns the part in the job by 90° about Z (seen from above) – so X runs along the edge you want; stock and origin follow.
ba.rohteil.text: A block around the part, with an allowance per side – like FreeCAD's job. Empty: 1 mm.
ba.rohteil.oben.tooltip: This much stock stands above the top of the part – face milling takes it off. Empty: 1 mm.
ba.rohteil.seite.tooltip: How far the stock reaches past the part on all four sides. Empty: 1 mm.
ba.rohteil.unten.tooltip: How far the stock reaches below the part. Empty: 1 mm.
ba.gespannt.tooltip: This much of the stock sits in the vise from below. “Check on machine” reports every path that goes below it beside the stock – where the jaws are – or below the stock. Empty: nothing checked.
ba.nullpunkt.text: Where X 0, Y 0, Z 0 of the program lie (the axes in the 3D view): as in the model, or a point of the stock – corner, edge middle, centre top or bottom –, shifted by X, Y, Z. Part and stock move so that the point lies at the origin.
ba.nullpunkt.wahl.tooltip: A point of the stock block: left/right is X, front/back Y, bottom/top Z. “As in the model” leaves the part where it lies in the model.
ba.nullpunkt.versatz.tooltip: How far the zero point lies from the chosen point – negative too. Empty: 0.
ba.flaechen.tooltip: Which faces are machined: flat ones facing up are milled flat (without a choice the top), walls get the contour. A click on a face of the part adds it, another click removes it.
ba.flaechen.liste.tooltip: The selected faces: green flat facing up (face milling) or wall (contour); red can take no machining. Double-click removes one.
ba.flaechen.oberseite: The top of the part ({namen}) – without a choice it is milled flat. Other faces and walls: click them in 3D.
ba.flaechen.nur: Only these faces: flat ones facing up are milled flat, the contour follows the walls.
ba.flaechen.oberseite_knopf.tooltip: Selects the highest flat faces of the part.
ba.flaeche.nichts: {name}  neither flat facing up nor a wall – no machining for it
ba.flaeche.schraeg: {name}  inclined {winkel}° – not in this job, swivelled yes (below)
ba.schwenken.text: {name} is inclined {winkel}°. On a 5-axis mill the machine swivels the plane, then mills there as from above:
ba.schwenken.erst_anlegen: {name} is inclined {winkel}°. On a 5-axis mill it can be done swivelled: first “Create”, then click the face and “Swivel plane (3+2) …”.
ba.schwenken.knopf.tooltip: Closes the assistant without creating anything and opens “Swivel plane” with this face – the plane becomes a job of its own, in which the assistant opens again.
ba.flaeche.fehlt: {name}  no longer exists in the part
ba.planfraesen.text: Mills the flat faces facing up flat: rows back and forth in layers from the stock down to the face plus allowance, with overrun past the edge, semicircles between the rows and half feed on exit; before steps the row stops.
ba.planfraeser.tooltip: A cutter with a flat tip from the tool manager with cutting data: flat, torus or face mill.
ba.planeinsatz.tooltip: Which cutting data of the cutter apply – preselected the application that is faster here: “Facing” (large ae, small ap) for a thin layer, “Roughing” for deep material. It gives speed, feed, stepdown (ap) and row spacing (ae).
ba.zustellung.tooltip: This deep per layer. Empty: the grey suggestion, ap of the application from the tool table.
ba.zeilenabstand.tooltip: How far the rows step across – at most as wide as the flat part of the tip. Empty: the grey suggestion, ae of the application.
ba.aufmass.tooltip: This much stays on the face; 0 finishes it.
ba.kontur.text: Follows the selected walls – outside around a boss, inside a pocket –, with tangential lead-in and lead-out, climb milling: roughing in layers with an allowance, as many passes side by side as material stands beside the wall, then finishing in one go over the full height.
ba.kontur.keine_wand: No wall selected – click a vertical face in 3D.
ba.konturfraeser.tooltip: A cutter with a flat tip from the tool manager with cutting data: flat, torus or face mill. Its radius sets the distance to the wall.
ba.kontureinsatz.tooltip: Which cutting data of the cutter apply – “Roughing” preselected. It gives speed, feed, stepdown (ap) and row spacing (ae).
ba.kontur.zustellung.tooltip: This deep per layer when roughing. Empty: the grey suggestion, ap of the application.
ba.kontur.zeilenabstand.tooltip: How far apart the roughing passes lie sideways, at most as wide as the cutter. Empty: the grey suggestion, ae of the application.
ba.aufmass_schlichten.tooltip: This much stays on the wall after roughing; the “Finishing” tick takes it off in one go. Empty: 0.3 mm.
ba.breite.tooltip: This much material stands beside the wall – that many roughing passes side by side. Empty: as much as the stock says – outside everything to the edge, a pocket completely.
ba.schlichten.tooltip: After roughing once along the wall at the cutter radius over the full height – at most the cutting edge length per go. Without the tick the allowance stays.
ba.ziel.mit: Target with {werkzeug}: {zeit} – on average ap {ap}, {anteil} % of its metal removal rate.
ba.ziel.rest: {rest} in corners and slots narrower than it remain for a smaller one.
ba.ziel.schneller: Faster from the tool box: {werkzeug} – target {zeit}.
ba.ziel.uebernehmen.tooltip: Puts the faster cutters from the target line into the strategies: a face mill into face milling and the one for the rest into clearing, an end mill into clearing and the one for the rest into rest material. Optional – whoever wants to mill everything with one cutter leaves it.
ba.ziel.tooltip: The target time, before any path is calculated: the volume between stock and part – without what the operations before it in the job have already removed –, at every spot in as many layers as the application's ap requires, at its ae and vf – as if the cutter were never out of the cut. Where it is shallow the cutter only uses part of its ap: a large face with little to remove takes long. Every path takes longer (air, plunging, rapids) – by how much tells how good it is. If another cutter from the tool box would be clearly faster, it is named after it.
ba.passt_nicht.zu: Click to see what to click in 3D for them.
ba.passt_nicht.offen: For them, click in 3D what it says next to each.
ba.passt_nicht.tooltip: The strategies that do not work with the selection in 3D. Opened, one line each: the name and what to click for it.
ba.unfertig: No exact final path – the part would not be as drawn there: {flaechen}. Tick for it: {bloecke}.
ba.unfertig.keiner: No exact final path – the part would not be as drawn there: {flaechen}. None of the strategies offered finishes them here.
an.eigenschaft.anstellen: Ball end mill tilted (5-axis simultaneous): the axis tilts only as far as needed about the centre of the ball, so it does not cut with its tip – the path stays the same.
an.eigenschaft.winkel: At least this far the tool axis stands off the surface (between axis and surface normal); steeper spots run vertical.
an.eigenschaft.kippachse: The tool tilts about this axis of the job – on the machine with one rotary axis, the other one stays.
an.eigenschaft.achsen: The tool axis per block of the path (computed).
an.nur_kugel: {operation}: tilting only works with a ball end mill – the path stays vertical.
an.fehler.kugel: “{operation}” is tilted but no longer has a ball end mill – please recompute.
an.fehler.veraltet: “{operation}”: the tool axes no longer match the path – please recompute.
pp.hinweis.angestellt_senkrecht: the ball end mill stands vertical – the program is tilted with a machine with two rotary axes (choose it above). The ball runs the same path, only it cuts with its tip on flat spots.
pp.hinweis.angestellt_fehler: written vertical – tilted it does not work on this machine: {grund}
si.fehler.achse: Point {punkt} of the path: there is no rotary-axis position for this tool axis.
si.fehler.grenze: Point {punkt} of the path: {achse} would have to go to {wert}° – outside its limits.
si.fehler.linear: The machine has no three linear axes for this tool – the path cannot be computed without TCPM.
sw.fehler.nicht_eben: {name} is neither flat nor the wall of a hole with an open end – a plane is tilted onto a flat face or into the axis of a hole.
sw.fehler.zyklus: Drilling cycles in this swivelled plane need the control's swivel cycle – the tool axis is not vertical in the program.
befehl.schwenken.tooltip: Click an inclined face on the part of a job: the machine swivels the plane with its rotary axes until the tool stands perpendicular on it – a job of its own in which every strategy computes as on a 3-axis machine.
sw.kein_job: First the part needs a job in a box – “Machining” creates it. Then click an inclined face on the part and “Swivel plane”.
sw.panel.text: Click a planar face on the part the tool is to stand perpendicular on – or the wall of an angled hole: then it stands in the hole’s axis. The part stays clamped as it lies in the base job; the rotary axes turn it (or the head). The plane becomes a job of its own – in it the face points up, and the “Machining” assistant mills there as on a 3-axis machine.
sw.panel.maschine: {maschine} – the rotary axes from its chain
sw.panel.ohne_maschine: none with two rotary axes – computed like an A table (about X) with rotary table C, pivot at the zero point
sw.panel.anklicken: click a flat face or the wall of a hole on the part …
sw.panel.waagerecht: {flaeche} lies horizontal – nothing to swivel; the base job does that.
sw.panel.vorhanden: This plane exists already: “{job}” – OK opens it instead of creating a second one.
sw.panel.neigung.tooltip: How far the tool tilts from the base job's vertical.
sw.panel.richtung.tooltip: Where the head tilts, seen from above: 0° towards +X, 90° towards +Y, −90° towards −Y.
sw.panel.winkel_knopf.tooltip: The plane from tilt and direction instead of a face – for a tilted ball end mill, say (3D finishing in the plane mills the same surface, only the ball no longer cuts with its tip) or a hole at an angle.
sw.panel.bearbeiten.tooltip: The assistant opens in the new job with the face selected – choose strategies and create as always.
pp.feld.bohren.tooltip: Instead of G81: per hole over the hole, then this command. {rtp} retract plane (G98: the height before, G99: R), {rfp} reference plane R, {dp} depth, {f} feed. Empty: G81 stays. If any drilling command is set, G80, G98 and G99 are left out.
pp.feld.bohren_verweilen.tooltip: Instead of G82 – like drilling, plus {dtb} the dwell at the bottom in seconds (P).
pp.feld.tiefbohren.tooltip: Instead of G83 – like drilling, plus {fdep} the first depth (R − Q) and {q} the infeed; fully out between pecks.
pp.feld.spaenebrechen.tooltip: Instead of G73 – like deep drilling, only a little back between pecks.
pp.feld.reiben.tooltip: Instead of G85 – in and out at feed {f}.
pp.haken.schwenkzyklus.erklaerung: A swivelled plane (a job with a plane): the control swivels with its cycle and computes rotary axes and tool length itself; the blocks are in plane coordinates. Off (or without command): the rotary axes are in the program, X, Y and Z computed for the rotated machine – first to the change point, afterwards the rotary axes to 0.
pp.feld.schwenken.tooltip: Before the operations of a swivelled plane. {x0} {y0} {z0}: the plane's origin in the base job, {a} {b} {c}: its angles axis by axis about Z, Y, X. Siemens: CYCLE800 with retract Z, the swivel data set between the quotes (empty: the only one) and direction −1.
pp.feld.schwenken_aus.tooltip: After the last operation of a swivelled plane and at the end of the program.
pp.hinweis.ebene_ohne_kette: The planes (3+2) are written without a swivel cycle, but the selected machine has no two rotary axes – computed as an A table (about X) with rotary table C, the pivot at the zero point. Select the 5-axis machine or the swivel cycle.
sw.fehler.ohne_maschine: Without swivel cycle the program needs the machine for the rotary axes {rundachsen} – without it only for an A, C table with the pivot at the zero point.
sw.fehler.keine_stellung: There is no position of the rotary axes for {flaeche} – the tool cannot stand perpendicular on the face.
sw.fehler.grenze: For {flaeche} the rotary axes would have to go to {rundachsen} – outside their limits.
sw.eigenschaft.grundjob: The job in which the part lies on the table as it is clamped – the machine swivels this plane from it.
sw.eigenschaft.ebene: The position of the plane in the base job: origin and axes; Z is the tool axis.
sw.eigenschaft.flaeche: The face of the base job's model the plane is swivelled onto.
sw.eigenschaft.rundachsen: The position of the rotary axes for this plane, computed from the machine.
ba.raeumen.ueberlastet: {text} – rings would be {prozent} % faster but overload the cutter (up to {last} ae)
ba.raeumen.haelt_nicht: {text} – no path keeps the load here (up to {last} ae): too narrow for this cutter
ba.raeumen.ausgelassen: {text}. The Ø {d} does not fit into pocket {flaeche} – it is left standing.
ba.raeumen.ausgelassen.mehrere: {text}. The Ø {d} does not fit into pockets {flaechen} – they are left standing.
ba.raeumen.ausgelassen.rest: {text}. The Ø {d} does not fit into pocket {flaeche} – “Clear the rest” clears it with {t}.
ba.raeumen.ausgelassen.rest.mehrere: {text}. The Ø {d} does not fit into pockets {flaechen} – “Clear the rest” clears them with {t}.
ba.restraeumen.text: Clears with a smaller cutter the pockets the clearing cutter does not fit into – like clearing, only there, right after it as an operation of its own. Preselected is the largest cutter in the tool manager that fits; the allowance stays on the walls.
ba.restraeumen.nicht: Only when the clearing cutter does not fit into a selected pocket – then a smaller one clears it here.
ba.schlichten_danach.text: After clearing, with a cutter of its own: first the floor – a clearing without floor allowance, in one layer –, then the walls around the cleared faces in the allowance, down to the finished floor; before that a measuring stop if wanted. Walls the contour runs, it finishes itself.
ba.schlichten_danach.fraeser.tooltip: The cutter for finishing – preselected the clearing cutter. Another one gets a tool controller of its own.
ba.schlichten_danach.einsatz.tooltip: Its cutting data – preselected “Finishing”: speed and feed for floor and walls, the stepdown for the walls.
ba.schlichten_danach.zustellung.tooltip: ap – this high is one layer at the wall; higher walls in several layers. Empty: the ap of the application.
ba.schlichten_danach.zeilenabstand.toolt: ae – this far apart the passes on the floor lie; the floor is thin, they may be wide apart. Empty: half the cutter diameter.
ba.schlichten_danach.boden_haken.tooltip: Finish the floor where clearing leaves a floor allowance – a clearing without floor allowance, in one layer. If it leaves none, there is nothing to do here.
ba.schlichten_danach.waende_haken.toolti: Run along the walls around the cleared faces in the allowance – bosses, islands, steps, pockets – down to the finished floor: a contour with width = allowance, only the pass along the wall.
ba.schlichten_danach.messstopp.tooltip: Before finishing the program stops: Z moves up, the spindle stops (M5, M0) – measure, then start; the spindle runs up again with the finishing speed. An operation of its own, “Measuring stop”.
ba.schlichten_danach.nichts: Nothing to finish here: clearing leaves no floor allowance, and there are no walls in the allowance – or the contour runs them.
ms.name: Measuring stop
ba.raeumen.text: Clears the flat upward faces like an HSM path: at full stepdown and a narrow stepover, without turning, climb milling – adaptive (the engagement stays at ae, it returns through the cleared area at depth instead of lifting) or with rings, whichever is faster and keeps the load. It plunges only where it is already free, otherwise it leads in tangentially from the free area (in a pocket down a helix). At walls and islands the allowance stays – for the contour.
ba.raeumfraeser.tooltip: The cutter for clearing – from the tool management, with a flat tip: end mill, torus or face mill.
ba.raeumeinsatz.tooltip: The application whose values apply: roughing first (narrow ae, full ap), otherwise facing or finishing.
ba.raeumen.zeilenabstand.tooltip: ae – how far the rings move inwards, at most the cutter radius. Empty: the ae of the application.
ba.aufmass_wand.tooltip: How much stays at walls and islands – the contour takes it afterwards. Empty: 0.3 mm.
ba.aufmass_boden.tooltip: How much stays on the face. Empty: 0 – the face is finished.
ba.gleichlauf.tooltip: The material lies to the right of the direction of travel (climb milling with a clockwise spindle, M3 – kind to edge and surface): clockwise around a boss, counter-clockwise in a pocket. Unchecked: conventional milling, the material to the left. With the tool controller set to “Reverse” (M4) the path runs the other way round.
ba.nur_gleichlauf.tooltip: On: every row climb milling – at its end the cutter lifts, rapids back and enters again at the start of the next. Off: back and forth, faster, but every other row conventional. With “Reverse” on the tool controller (M4) the direction turns with it.
ba.raeumen.keine_flaeche: No flat upward face and no pocket wall selected – clearing needs a top face or a pocket floor.
ba.wettbewerb.schnellste_knapp: {text} – the fastest; {andere} would be less than 1 % slower
ba.wettbewerb.vollschnitt: {text} – in the slot it would first cut full width, more than ae; the slot strategy mills it in arcs
ba.kontur.nach_planen: {text} – only the rest at the walls: face milling mills the floor in front
ba.kontur.nach_raeumen: {text} – only the allowance at the walls: clearing clears the pocket
ba.kontur.nach_raeumen_boden: {text} – only the allowance at the walls: clearing clears the floor in front
ba.wettbewerb.folge: {text} – with clearing of the pocket floors the fastest sequence; clearing everything would be {prozent} % slower
ba.wettbewerb.nur_boeden: {text} – only the pocket floors, face milling does the flat faces
ba.wettbewerb.folge_langsamer: {text} – with clearing of the pocket floors {prozent} % slower than clearing everything
ba.wettbewerb.alles: {text} – everything, the fastest sequence; face milling plus clearing the floors would be {prozent} % slower
ba.richtung.langsamer: {text} – rows along {richtung}; along {andere} it would be {prozent} % slower
ba.anlegen.tooltip: Creates the tool controllers and the ticked operations in the job – one undo step (job and stock a second one).
ba.uebernehmen.tooltip: Changes the operation: faces, cutter, application and the values – one undo step.
rw.werkzeug_radial: “{operation}”: the path is calculated for a tool pointing radially at the axis from {richtung} – but {werkzeug} on {aufnahme} sits differently. Run like this, it does not fit the part: give {werkzeug} a holder in the tool manager that stands radially (such as “VDI30 driven radial”), or use a station pointing from {richtung}.
rw.werkzeug_radial_gerade: “{operation}”: the path is calculated for a tool pointing radially at the axis from {richtung} – but {werkzeug} on {aufnahme} sits differently. Run like this, it does not fit the part: {aufnahme} itself stands radially – give {werkzeug} a straight holder in the tool manager.
dialog.verfahrweg.lage_nur_von: At the “from” limit it is {von}; “to” has no limit.
dialog.verfahrweg.lage_nur_bis: At the “to” limit it is {bis}; “from” has no limit.
dialog.home.tooltip: Where the axis is when the machine is at home – counted like the travel. If an axis has a home position, traversing in the check window starts and ends there, and before every tool change the machine moves to the change position: first Z up (on a lathe X away), then the other axes; back the other axes first, then Z. Empty: no home position – traversing starts at the first point of the path.
dialog.punkte.leer: No linear axis yet – as soon as X, Y or Z has an operating mode “Linear”, its points show here.
dialog.wechsel_bezug.wks: WCS – workpiece coordinates (tool tip, from the job's zero point)
dialog.wechsel_bezug.tooltip: MCS: for a tool change the axes go to fixed spots of the machine (G53 in the program, SUPA on Siemens) – independent of workpiece and tool. WCS: the tool tip goes to a spot from the job's zero point (G0 in the program); axes without a value stay. Home always counts in MCS.
eigenschaft.wechselzeit: How long a tool change itself takes (s) – “Check on machine” counts it per change; 0: not counted.
dialog.wechselzeit.tooltip: Measured chip to chip on the machine, or from the data sheet (“chip-to-chip time”). “Check on machine” adds it to the time at every change; empty: not counted.
eigenschaft.wechsel_bezug: What the tool change point counts in: MCS (machine coordinates, like the travel) or WCS (workpiece coordinates, from the job's zero point).
pp.maschine.ohne_wechselpunkt: no change point – in “Edit machine” under “Home and tool change”
pp.feld.wechselpunkt_mks.tooltip: Before every tool change and at the end: to the machine's change point in machine coordinates. {achsen} are the axes with their positions – first alone the axis that pulls the tool away. Without {achsen} the command appears once – e.g. F_HOME (ShopTurn) or the builder's M codes.
pp.feld.wechselpunkt_wks.tooltip: As above, when the change point counts in workpiece coordinates: a rapid in the program.
dialog.wechsel.tooltip: Where the axis is for the tool change – counted like the travel. Empty: at the home position.
dialog.grenze.tooltip: How far the axis may move – the limit on the assembly joint. Empty: no limit.
dialog.verfahrweg.null: Counted as on the joint: the position of the slide, not the tool tip.
dialog.schwenkbereich.null: Counted as on the joint, in degrees; does not apply while “endless” is ticked.
dialog.verfahrweg.lage: {achse} is now at {stellung}; {aufnahme} is {abstand} away from the workpiece mount (along {achse}).
dialog.verfahrweg.lage_grenzen: At the limits it is {von} and {bis}.
dialog.verfahrweg.spitze: Where the tip gets to with a tool is shown by “Check on machine”.
bo.name: Hole milling {werkzeug}
bo.eigenschaft.flaechen: The cylindrical faces of the holes (“Face7” …); empty: all holes of the part.
bo.eigenschaft.zustellung: At most this deep per layer – only in holes larger than two cutters (rings outwards there); smaller ones the helix mills in one go.
bo.eigenschaft.zeilenabstand: ae – this far the rings step outwards in large holes.
bo.eigenschaft.aufmass: Stays on the wall after roughing – finishing takes it.
bo.eigenschaft.schlichten: Then the wall at the radius in one go, with half circles in from the middle and out again.
bo.eigenschaft.tiefer: This far below the bottom of a through hole, so no burr remains.
bo.eigenschaft.eintauchwinkel: This steep the helix goes down (degrees) – from the tool.
bo.eigenschaft.umlaeufe: Turns of the helix over all holes (result).
bo.fehler.form: Hole milling needs a cutter with a flat end – end, torus or face mill.
bo.fehler.werte: Stepdown and row spacing must be greater than 0.
bo.fehler.keine: No hole selected – click the cylindrical face of a hole in the 3D view.
bo.fehler.zu_klein: The hole Ø {durchmesser} is smaller than the cutter – a smaller cutter or a drill.
bo.fehler.nichts: Nothing stands above the holes – the stock ends at their bottom.
ba.bohrung.text: Mills cylindrical holes with an end mill smaller than them: down in a helix (G2/G3 with Z, as steep as the tool's plunge angle), in large holes rings outwards per layer, then the wall finished in one go – climb milling, with half circles in from the middle and out. No drill needed; through holes 0.5 mm deeper.
ba.bohrfraeser.tooltip: A cutter with a flat end, smaller than the hole.
ba.bohrung.zustellung.tooltip: ap per layer – only for holes larger than two cutters; smaller ones the helix mills in one go. Empty: the ap of the application.
ba.bohrung.zeilenabstand.tooltip: ae – this far the rings step outwards in large holes. Empty: the ae of the application.
ba.bohrung.keine: No hole selected – click the cylindrical face of a hole in the 3D view.
ba.wand_schlichten.tooltip: After roughing the wall at the radius in one go – without the tick the helix mills to size directly.
nt.name: Slot {werkzeug}
nt.eigenschaft.flaechen: Walls or floor of the slots (“Face7” …) – one face per slot is enough.
nt.eigenschaft.zustellung: At most this deep per layer of arcs (ap); at full width at most half the diameter.
nt.eigenschaft.zeilenabstand: ae – it gives the step of the arcs: so far that the cutter wraps the dent no further than a straight wall with ae.
nt.eigenschaft.schlichten: Afterwards the wall once all round, with semicircles from the centre of one end in and out again.
nt.eigenschaft.tiefer: This far it mills below the floor of a through slot, so no burr is left.
nt.eigenschaft.eintauchwinkel: This steep the helix and the ramp go down (degrees) – from the tool.
nt.eigenschaft.boegen: Arcs over all slots and layers (result).
nt.fehler.form: Slot needs a cutter with a flat end – end mill, bull-nose or face mill.
nt.fehler.werte: Stepdown and row spacing must be greater than 0.
nt.fehler.keine: No slot selected – click a wall or the floor of a slot in the 3D view.
nt.fehler.zu_schmal: The slot is {breite} wide, the cutter Ø {fraeser} – use a narrower cutter.
nt.fehler.zu_breit: The slot is {breite} wide – nearly two cutters: a core would stay in the middle of the helix. A larger cutter, or “Clearing”.
nt.fehler.nichts: Nothing stands above the slots – the stock ends at their floor.
ba.nut.text: Mills slots with an end mill no wider than they are – never at full width with the whole flute: if the slot is wider than the cutter, in arcs – each arc climb milling from wall to wall, back across the free side at high feed –, in layers of ap; a closed slot after a helix at one end, an open one (running out at the edge) from outside, then at any width. If it is barely wider, in a zigzag ramp along the slot. Finally the wall once all round – climb milling; through slots 0.5 mm deeper.
ba.nutfraeser.tooltip: A cutter with a flat end, narrower than the slot – fastest at 50 to 75 % of its width.
ba.nuteinsatz.tooltip: The cutting data – preselected “Dynamic roughing” or “Roughing” (small ae, whole flute); if the slot is barely wider than the cutter, “Full slot”.
ba.nut.zustellung.tooltip: ap per layer of arcs; at full width (ramp) at most half the diameter. Empty: the ap of the application.
ba.nut.zeilenabstand.tooltip: ae – it gives the step of the arcs: so far that the cutter wraps the dent no further than a straight wall with ae (in narrow slots part of it). Empty: the ae of the application.
ba.nut.keine: No slot selected – click a wall or the floor of a slot in the 3D view.
ba.ergebnis_vollnut: → {nuten} at full width with a ramp, about {zeit}
rb.name: Reaming {werkzeug}
rb.fehler.keine: No hole selected – click the wall of a hole in the 3D view.
rb.fehler.durchmesser: The reamer Ø {reibahle} does not fit the hole Ø {durchmesser} – add a reamer with this diameter in the tool management.
rb.fehler.sack: The hole Ø {durchmesser} has a flat bottom – no drill can pre-drill it; through holes and blind holes with a drill tip are reamed.
bh.fehler.vorbohren: Before reaming a smaller drill pre-drills: for Ø {durchmesser} one with Ø {von} to {bis} – this one has Ø {bohrer}.
ba.reiben.text: Reams holes to size with a reamer of their diameter – FreeCAD's Drilling with G85: in at feed and out again at feed. Through holes 1 mm below the bottom, blind holes with a drill tip to the bottom of the wall. Pre-drilling is smaller: with the tick “Drilling” drills 0.15 to 0.5 mm undersize, and “Hole milling” and the contour do not compete in these holes. You set the tick yourself.
ba.reibahle.tooltip: A reamer with the diameter of the hole.
ba.reiben.nicht: For through holes and blind holes with a drill tip, when the tool management has a reamer with their diameter.
ba.bohrung.gerieben: The holes are reamed – pre-drilled with the drill, smaller than they are; milled they would already be to size.
s3.name: 3D finishing {werkzeug}
s3.eigenschaft.flaechen: The freeform faces (“Face7” …) – curved or sloped, facing up.
s3.eigenschaft.grathoehe: At most this high the ridges between two rows remain (measured on a flat face) – the row spacing follows from it.
s3.eigenschaft.aufmass: Remains on the faces – 0 for the finished size.
s3.eigenschaft.richtung: The rows along X, along Y, a spiral from the centre outwards or curves along the face (“flaeche”) or rings at equal spacing in space (“aequidistant”); “auto”: the fastest.
s3.eigenschaft.zeilen: Rows with a cut, along the face the curves, equidistant the rings (result).
s3.eigenschaft.davor: Rest finishing: the diameter of the larger cutter that finished before – 0: finish everything.
s3.eigenschaft.eckenradius_davor: Rest finishing: the corner radius of the cutter before – ball Ø/2, flat end mill 0.
rs.name: Rest finishing {werkzeug}
ba.rs.text: Finishes with a smaller cutter only where the larger one before could not reach – in fillets, tight curves and corners of the freeform faces. Where the rest lies is computed from both cutters: the surface the large one left against the one the small one reaches. There rows, contour lines or a spiral as in 3D finishing, the fastest counts. After 3D finishing; you set the tick yourself.
ba.rs.fraeser.tooltip: A ball end mill (best) or bull nose, smaller than the one before – preselected the largest smaller one.
ba.rs.davor.tooltip: The diameter of the cutter that finished the faces before – empty: the one of 3D finishing in this window (then with its shape); entered by hand it counts as a ball end mill.
ba.rs.davor.fehlt: Which cutter was before? Enter its Ø – or tick 3D finishing with the large cutter.
ba.rs.keine: No freeform face selected – click a curved or sloped face in 3D.
s3.eigenschaft.abstand: The row spacing from the scallop height (result).
s3.fehler.form: 3D finishing needs a cutter whose shape the add-on knows – ball, bull-nose or end mill.
s3.fehler.grathoehe: The scallop height must be greater than 0.
s3.fehler.keine: No freeform face selected – click a curved or sloped face in the 3D view.
s3.fehler.kein_rest: No rest: the cutter before left nothing this one would remove – choose a smaller cutter or other faces.
s3.fehler.nichts: There is nothing to mill on the selected faces – other faces keep the cutter above them.
ba.s3.text: Finishes freeform faces – domes, fillets, slopes –, the tip on the envelope of the whole part: the cutter touches the selected faces and never cuts into the part, not into neighbouring faces either. It mills only where it touches the selected faces and they set its height. The row spacing follows from the scallop height; rows along X and along Y, a spiral, curves along the face and rings at equal spacing (equidistant) are computed, the fastest counts. Best with a ball end mill, after roughing.
ba.s3.fraeser.tooltip: A ball end mill (best), bull-nose or end mill.
ba.grathoehe.tooltip: At most this high the ridges between two rows remain (on a flat face) – smaller: finer, but more rows. Empty: 0.01 mm.
ba.s3.aufmass.tooltip: This much remains on the faces, measured normal to the face; 0 finishes them.
ba.s3.keine: No freeform face selected – click a curved or sloped face in the 3D view.
s3.eigenschaft.grenzwinkel: Steep/shallow: where it is steeper (degrees) it runs contours, where shallower rows; 0: rows only.
ba.ergebnis_s3_spirale_steil: → {n} contours and a spiral with {umlaeufe}, spacing {abstand}, about {zeit}
r3.name: 3D roughing {werkzeug}
r3.eigenschaft.flaechen: The freeform faces (“Face7” …) above which the stock is cleared – curved or sloped, facing up.
r3.eigenschaft.aufmass: Allowance: this much stays on the faces, normal to them, and on the floor below – for 3D finishing.
r3.eigenschaft.zwischenlagen: Intermediate layers: this far apart (mm) they clear the steps between the layers above the faces – at most this high they remain; 0: none.
r3.fehler.keine: No freeform face selected – click a curved or sloped face in the 3D view.
r3.eigenschaft.davor: Rest roughing: the diameter of the larger cutter that roughed before – 0: the whole stock.
r3.eigenschaft.eckenradius_davor: Rest roughing: the corner radius of the cutter before – flat end mill 0.
rr.name: Rest roughing {werkzeug}
ba.rr.text: Roughs with a smaller cutter only what the larger one before left – in narrow gaps between freeform faces, in corners and fillets it could not get down into. What remains is computed from its envelope: as deep as its flat face got. There layers as in 3D roughing, only where material stands. After 3D roughing; you set the tick yourself.
ba.rr.fraeser.tooltip: A cutter with a flat face, smaller than the one before – preselected the largest smaller one.
ba.rr.davor.tooltip: The diameter of the cutter that roughed before – empty: the one of 3D roughing in this window (then with its shape); entered by hand it counts as a flat end mill.
ba.rr.davor.fehlt: Which cutter was before? Enter its Ø – or tick 3D roughing with the large cutter.
r3.fehler.kein_rest: No rest: the cutter before left nothing this one reaches – choose a smaller cutter or other faces.
r3.fehler.nichts: Nothing stands above the selected faces – the stock ends on them, or the cutter cannot reach them.
ba.r3.text: Clears the stock above freeform faces – in layers at full flute length with a narrow ae like Clearing, with intermediate layers only where a step still stands above the face. The allowance remains, and steps at most as high as the intermediate layers are apart – for 3D finishing afterwards.
ba.r3.fraeser.tooltip: The cutter for roughing – from the tool management, with a flat tip: end mill or torus.
ba.r3.einsatz.tooltip: The application whose values apply: roughing first (narrow ae, full ap), otherwise facing or finishing.
ba.r3.aufmass.tooltip: This much stays on the faces, measured normal to them, and on the floor below – for 3D finishing.
ba.zwischenlagen.tooltip: This far apart the intermediate layers clear the steps above the faces – at most this high they remain; 0: no intermediate layers.
ba.r3.keine: No freeform face selected – click a curved or sloped face in the 3D view.
bs.name: Pencil {werkzeug}
bs.eigenschaft.laenge: Length of the path on the fillets (result).
bs.fehler.form: The pencil pass needs a cutter whose shape the add-on knows – preferably a ball end mill.
bs.fehler.keine_kehle: There is no fillet at the selected faces – nowhere does the cutter touch two faces at once.
ba.bs.text: Traces the fillets of freeform faces: where the ball end mill touches the selected face and its neighbour at once – at the foot of a dome, in a groove. The rows of 3D finishing end there and leave a rest between their ends; the pencil pass takes it in one go. After 3D finishing, with the same ball end mill. You set the tick yourself.
ba.bs.fraeser.tooltip: A ball end mill (best) – or a bull-nose.
ba.bs.aufmass.tooltip: This much stays in the fillet, measured normal to the faces; 0 finishes it.
ba.bs.keine: No freeform face selected – click a curved or sloped face in the 3D view.
bh.name: Drilling {werkzeug}
bh.fehler.keine: No hole selected – click the wall of a hole in the 3D view.
bh.fehler.sack: The hole Ø {durchmesser} has a flat bottom – a drill would leave its tip; “Hole milling” mills it.
bh.fehler.spitze: The blind hole Ø {durchmesser} has a tip of {spitze}° at the bottom – the drill has {winkel}°; take a drill with its angle.
bh.fehler.durchmesser: The drill Ø {bohrer} does not fit the hole Ø {durchmesser} – create a drill with this diameter in the tool management.
ba.bohren.text: Drills holes with a drill from the tool management that has their diameter – through holes and blind holes with the tip of its angle (FreeCAD's Hole draws it with 118°). FreeCAD's Drilling (G81, deeper than 3 × D in pecks with G83); the tip goes its length below the bottom of the wall: the hole has the full diameter all the way down, in a blind hole the tip sits where the model has it.
ba.bohren.nicht: For through holes and blind holes with a drill tip, when the tool management has a drill with their diameter (and the angle of the tip).
ba.bohrer.tooltip: A drill from the tool management – preselected the one with the diameter of the hole.
ba.bohren.hub.tooltip: This deep per peck, then back to R to break the chip (G83). Empty: deeper than 3 × D 1 × D each, shallower in one go (G81).
gw.name: Thread {gewinde} {werkzeug}
gw.fehler.keine: No hole selected – click the wall of the core hole in the 3D view.
gw.fehler.kernloch: {gewinde} needs a core hole Ø {kern} – the hole has Ø {durchmesser}.
gw.fehler.steigung: The tap has no pitch – enter it in the tool management.
gf.name: Thread milling {werkzeug}
gf.eigenschaft.flaechen: The cylindrical faces of the core holes (“Face7” …); empty: all holes of the part.
gf.eigenschaft.steigung: The pitch of the thread mill (mm per turn) – from the tool management. With it and the core hole the thread is fixed (Ø 8.5 with 1.5 → M10 × 1.5).
gf.eigenschaft.zaehne: This many teeth the cutter has stacked (from the cutting length). It mills this many turns at once and needs only as many revolutions as it takes for the top tooth to reach the top. 1: one tooth, turn by turn.
gf.eigenschaft.links: Left-hand thread: the helix the other way round.
gf.eigenschaft.durchgaenge: In this many steps outwards (equal chip area per step) – more for a large pitch in tough material.
gf.eigenschaft.korrektur: This much larger (on the diameter) it mills the thread than the middle of tolerance 6H – after the gauge: if the go side does not enter, a little more.
gf.eigenschaft.umlaeufe: Turns of the helix over all threads (result).
gf.fehler.keine: No hole selected – click the wall of the core hole in the 3D view.
gf.fehler.fraeser: The thread mill has no diameter – enter it in the tool management.
gf.fehler.steigung: The thread mill has no pitch – enter it in the tool management.
gf.fehler.steigung_unbekannt: No metric thread has the pitch {steigung} – check the pitch of the thread mill.
gf.fehler.kein_gewinde: The hole Ø {durchmesser} is no core hole for a thread with pitch {steigung} – {gewinde} needs Ø {von} to {bis}.
gf.fehler.zu_gross: The thread mill Ø {fraeser} is too large for the hole Ø {durchmesser} – at most Ø {hoechstens}.
gf.fehler.korrektur: With this correction the cutter does not reach beyond the core hole for {gewinde} – check the correction.
gf.fehler.hals: The neck of the thread mill (Ø {hals}) is too thick for {gewinde} – at most Ø {hoechstens}, otherwise it rubs the crests of the thread.
gf.fehler.flach: The blind hole Ø {durchmesser} is too shallow for a thread – at least {tiefe} deep.
gf.fehler.reichweite: The thread mill reaches only {reichweite} below the shank – the thread needs {tiefe}.
ba.gewindefraesen.text: Mills metric internal threads with a thread mill from the tool management in holes with the core hole of a thread of its pitch (Ø 8.5 with pitch 1.5 → M10 × 1.5; tolerance 6H, milled to its middle). Per hole down in the middle, in on a half circle, the helix, back on a half circle – climb milling, the feed applies at the cutting edge. A cutter with several teeth needs only a few turns. The core hole is made before by drilling or hole milling; instead of tapping. You set the tick yourself.
ba.gewindefraesen.nicht: For holes with the core hole of a metric thread – with a thread mill of its pitch from the tool management, smaller than the core hole.
ba.gewindefraeser.tooltip: A thread mill from the tool management – preselected one whose pitch suits the selected core holes and which fits into them.
ba.gewindefraesen_einsatz.tooltip: The cutting data – “Thread milling” preselected; the feed applies at the cutting edge, the centre of the cutter moves correspondingly slower on the small circle.
ba.gewinde.text: Cuts threads with a tap from the tool management in holes with its core hole (thread Ø − pitch: M10 × 1.5 → Ø 8.5) – FreeCAD's Tapping (G84, left-hand G74). The core hole is made before by drilling or hole milling; through a through hole the tap goes its chamfer beyond, in a blind hole it stays one pitch above the bottom. You set the tick yourself.
ba.gewinde.nicht: For holes with the core hole of a tap from the tool management (M10 × 1.5: Ø 8.5).
ba.gewindebohrer.tooltip: A tap from the tool management – preselected the one whose core hole the hole has.
ba.gewinde_einsatz.tooltip: The cutting data – “Tapping” preselected; the feed is pitch · speed.
eg.name: Deburr {werkzeug}
eg.eigenschaft.flaechen: The selected faces: walls – their top edges get the chamfer – or flat faces facing up – then the edges where a wall goes down from them.
eg.eigenschaft.breite: Chamfer width: this wide the chamfer becomes on the top face (with a 90° chamfer mill it reaches as far down the wall).
eg.eigenschaft.tiefer: This much deeper than the chamfer stands the tip: the cone cuts the chamfer, not the tip, and the tip stays away from the wall.
eg.eigenschaft.einfahrradius: The quarter circle on which the cutter moves tangentially onto the edge and away again.
eg.eigenschaft.ketten: This many edge runs the operation machines (computed).
eg.eigenschaft.ausgelassen: This many edge runs the cutter does not reach – the wall is lower than the chamfer, or a step is in the way (computed).
eg.fehler.keine: The selected faces have no top edge to deburr and no modelled chamfer or rounding – click a wall, a chamfer, or the flat face on top at whose edge a wall goes down.
eg.fehler.winkel: The modelled chamfer needs a chamfer mill with {fase}° – this one has {fraeser}°.
eg.fehler.radius: The modelled rounding R {rundung} needs a corner rounding mill with this radius – this one has R {fraeser}.
eg.fehler.viertel: The hollow of the corner rounding mill is no full quarter circle (the pilot is wider than Ø − 2 × radius) – a step would remain on top.
eg.fehler.breite: The chamfer width must be greater than 0.
eg.fehler.form: Deburring needs a chamfer mill (chamfer) or a corner rounding mill (rounding).
eg.fehler.zu_breit: The chamfer is wider than the cone of the chamfer mill cuts – at most {hoechstens}; a narrower chamfer or a larger chamfer mill.
eg.fehler.nichts: The cutter reaches none of the edges: the walls are lower than the chamfer, or steps and other walls are in the way.
eg.ausgelassen: {anzahl} edge runs the cutter does not reach (the wall is lower than the chamfer, or a step is in the way) – see the property “Ausgelassen”.
ba.entgraten.text: Breaks the top edges of the selected walls with a chamfer mill or rounds them with a corner rounding mill – with a flat face selected, its edges where a wall goes down (outer edges, rims of pockets and holes): one path beside the edge, climb milling, tangentially in and out; the cone cuts the chamfer as wide as given, the rounding mill rounds with its radius. If the model already has the chamfer or rounding (click it, or the face on top), its sizes come from the model, and the tick is proposed. Comes last, when the edges are finished.
ba.entgraten.nicht: For top edges of walls and modelled chamfers and roundings, with a chamfer or corner rounding mill from the tool management – click a wall, a chamfer, a rounding or a flat face on top.
ba.fasenfraeser.tooltip: A chamfer or corner rounding mill from the tool management – at modelled chamfers and roundings the one that suits them is preselected.
ba.entgraten.breite.tooltip: This wide the chamfer becomes on the top face; with a 90° chamfer mill it reaches as far down the wall. Modelled chamfers keep their width from the model.
ba.entgraten.tiefer.tooltip: This much deeper than the chamfer stands the tip: the cone cuts the chamfer, not the tip, and the tip stays away from the wall.
ba.ergebnis_entgraten_ausgelassen: → {zuege}, about {zeit}; {ausgelassen} the cutter does not reach
zt.name: Spot drill {werkzeug}
zt.fehler.keine: No hole selected – click the wall of the hole in the 3D view.
sk.name: Countersink {werkzeug}
sk.fehler.keine: No countersink selected – click the conical face above the hole in the 3D view.
sk.fehler.winkel: The countersink tool has {senker}°, the countersink {senkung}° – create one with this angle in the tool management.
sk.fehler.durchmesser: The countersink tool Ø {senker} is smaller than the countersink Ø {senkung} – a larger one.
ba.zentrieren.text: Spots with an NC spot drill from the tool management before the drill comes – so deep that a small chamfer remains on top (Ø hole + 0.4 mm): the drill starts guided. FreeCAD's Drilling (G81); comes before drilling. You set the tick yourself.
ba.zentrieren.nicht: For holes, with an NC spot drill from the tool management – click the wall of a hole.
ba.anbohrer.tooltip: An NC spot drill from the tool management – its tip angle decides how deep it goes.
ba.senken.text: Countersinks with a countersink tool from the tool management the countersinks the model has – so deep that its cone has the Ø of the countersink on top. FreeCAD's Drilling (G81), after drilling.
ba.senken.nicht: For countersinks (the conical face above a hole), with a countersink tool of their angle from the tool management.
ba.senker.tooltip: A countersink tool from the tool management – preselected the one with the angle of the countersink.
zt.eigenschaft.fase: This wide is the chamfer spot drilling leaves on top of the hole (computed) – “Check on the machine” lets it pass.
ko.eigenschaft.radius_davor: Rest material: the radius of the cutter before – the path only runs where it did not reach (inner corners, narrow spots). 0: a whole contour.
rm.name: Rest material {werkzeug}
rm.fehler.nicht_groesser: The cutter before must be larger than this one – otherwise there is no rest material for it.
rm.fehler.nichts: The cutter before reached everywhere – no rest material remains at these walls.
ba.rest.text: Takes with a smaller cutter what the large one left at the selected walls – in inner corners and at spots narrower than it: one path beside the wall, only where the small one sticks out of the large one's way, in layers, climb milling, tangentially in and out. Comes after the contour. The assistant sets the tick when drawn inner fillets are smaller than the contour's cutter and a smaller one is there.
ba.rest.nicht: For walls, after a larger cutter – click the walls the contour runs along.
ba.restfraeser.tooltip: A cutter with a flat face from the tool management, smaller than the one before – the largest smaller one preselected.
ba.rest.davor.tooltip: The diameter of the cutter that ran along the walls before – empty: the one of the contour (or clearing) in this window.
ba.rest.davor.fehlt: Which cutter came before? Enter its Ø – or tick the contour with the large cutter.
ba.rest.zustellung.tooltip: This deep per layer (ap) – empty: from the application.
ms.fehler.schon_weg: Nothing left to do here – {wer} already removed it.
ms.eigenschaft.materialstand: What the material state was computed from: the stock and the operations before (if anything before changes, the operation recomputes)
ba.dazu.keine: Into the job “{job}” (no operation yet): machine, stock and origin stay as they are there.
ba.dazu.eine: Into the job “{job}” – 1 operation: {name}. Machine, stock and origin stay as they are there; the new operations come after it and take into account what is already removed.
ba.dazu.mehrere: Into the job “{job}” – {n} operations, last {name}. Machine, stock and origin stay as they are there; the new operations come after them and take into account what is already removed.
ba.neuer_job.tooltip: Create a new job instead of using this one – for a second setup, for example with the part turned over. You then choose machine, stock and origin again.
ba.anleitung.dazu: The part already has a job – “Next” to what should go.
nt.eigenschaft.eintauchstellen: Where the helix plunges into the slot – per slot (name of its first wall) the fraction from one end to the other (0 … 1); without an entry the suggestion
ba.nut.eintauchen.tooltip: Where the helix plunges into the slot – in every layer there. The suggestion: where the least material is (a hole or pocket crosses the slot), otherwise alternating at the ends.
ba.nut.im_bild.tooltip: Then click a point on the floor or a wall of the slot – the helix moves there.
ba.nut.vorschlag.stelle: Suggestion: X {x} Y {y} – least material there
